cases.object: V1 Exercise 23.7, A commuting square which is too small
cases.evidence_level: Actual rendered PDF inspection plus source read; local mathematical sanity check only
cases.observed_before: P2 has the statement and solution together. P3 leaves the statement at the end of PDF p103 and moves only its short solution to PDF p104.
cases.observed_after: v8 PDF p109 has the complete Exercise23.7 statement immediately followed by its complete solution. The page also contains the preceding Exercise23.6 solution; it is no longer an isolated page containing only the short Exercise23.7 solution.
local_math_checked: For f=b=id on a singleton and m=id_X, f_*m and b^*(f_*m) are whole-singleton subobjects.
The pullback of id_X along a:empty->X is represented by id_empty; its direct image under f_prime:empty->singleton is empty.
The two identity maps from a singleton form a compatible pair but cannot factor through empty X_prime.
The source explicitly retains X=Y=Y_prime={*}, f=b=id, X_prime=empty, the two unique maps, and m=id_X.
cases.neighbor_limitation: v8 Exercise23.6 is stated on p108 and solved on p109. This audit does not claim every exercise/solution pair is kept on one page. The shorter p109 is a chapter-end page, not evidence that every short page is bad or that every continuation is optimal.
cases.inference: The observed repair removes a specific need to turn a page solely for this short solution; explicit typed expressions also expose the two sides of the failed base-change equation.
not_established: The isolated causal effect of this repair on the user score
Whether the user rated this exact page
